titlePlain: Capstone: Map ITIL 4 Practices to a Real
subtitle: Lesson 28 · Applying ITIL 4 on a Real Platform

code:
Meridian Health Partners
  ~2,000 employees, HQ + six regional offices
  Claims processing + patient scheduling + office IT
  12-person service desk, small infra team, a CAB

Dec 15 - Jan 2: annual year-end change freeze.
An ordinary week lands five situations on IT's desk.
caption: Map each situation to the practice that owns it before reading on.

steps.label: VPN gateway down (4th time)
steps.sub: incident restores access now; problem management investigates the recurring cause

steps.label: New-hire laptop request
steps.sub: a service request fulfilled through the Service Catalog, not an incident

steps.label: Security patch during the freeze
steps.sub: change enablement's emergency change path -- authorized even during a freeze

steps.label: Tech escalates simple resets
steps.sub: a knowledge management and service desk gap, not an individual failure

steps.label: Post-freeze incident review
steps.sub: continual improvement turns a recurring pattern into a planned fix

code:
Every ticket above runs against SLA timers
  -> service level management

The laptop in Situation 2 is tracked from order
to retirement -> IT asset management

A real week doesn't label its tickets by practice.
Recognizing which one (or more) owns each ticket
is the skill this course built.
caption: Service level and asset management rarely get their own ticket -- they're underneath all of them.
